The identifier is a version 7 UUID: its first 48 bits are the session’s start in Unix milliseconds,
which every record’s timestamp sends anyway, and the rest is random, derived from nothing. It lives
in the enricher’s memory only.
Neither the tracker nor its store writes it to disk (a store keeps no record’s context), and the
next launch’s tracker starts a new session with a new identifier. Traffluent keeps no identifier
that links one session to another.
Every event can carry what most analytics want beside it: the app, the device, the operating
system, the locale and the network connection (module
: every platform). Each
is an enricher of its own, so nothing is added until the app adds it:

code: tracker.track(SignedUp(plan: "pro"))  // its record's context[OperatingSystemKey.self]?.name is "iOS" on an iPhone

abstract.text: Traffluent knows people only by a pseudonymous session. An identifier that outlives one is yours to add, store, reset and gate with consent.
Vendor-neutral analytics for Swift: typed events, tracked by a tracker and delivered in batches to any number of destinations.
Keep each record on disk until it is delivered, so a record the app tracked survives the process ending.
Derive an event’s conformances and schema from its declaration with
, and constrain which values its properties may hold.
Deliver an event only once the user grants the purpose it is collected for.
Track screen views, control activations and the app’s lifecycle without a call at each place they happen.

abstract.text: Export the JSON Schema of every event an app tracks, commit it, and fail the build when the events stop matching it.
Deliver events to your logs, your traces, a server or memory, and decide what each destination may see.
Keep a seeded fraction of the events a tracker tracks, event by event or a whole session at once.
